prompt: rustdoc doc auto_cfg hide default hidden cfg attributes
answer:
`rustdoc`’s `doc(auto_cfg)` hides these cfg predicates by default:

- `test`
- `doc`
- `doctest`

The current rustdoc implementation initializes its hidden set with those three predicates: [`CfgInfo::default`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/2972b5e5/src/librustdoc/clean/cfg.rs).

To hide additional predicates, use:

```rust
#![doc(auto_cfg(hide(unix)))]
```

This hides `unix` from automatically generated cfg markers for the crate’s items and descendants. Multiple predicates can be specified:

```rust
#![doc(auto_cfg(hide(unix, windows, feature = "internal")))]
```

`auto_cfg(hide(...))` affects automatically generated cfg information, not explicit `#[doc(cfg(...))]` attributes. It accepts only identifiers or key/value items, not expressions such as `not(unix)`.
